findings.claim: Unbounded D(u) forces inf_{Z^2} F=-infinity by choosing v=-q(u) after polynomial division with integer q.
assumptions_checked: G4=16(u+2v)^2, G3=32v(u+2v) integral quadratic, neither divisible by H

linked gcd condition and positive F2 on both quartic zero directions

global integer nonnegativity proved by parity and involution, not inferred from a grid
findings.decisive_evidence: The unique q=u/2-1/4 is never integral at integer u; h=16u+8. Off-lattice evaluation F(u,-q(u))=1-u(u+1) contrasts with F>=0 on Z^2. At u=20 the true integer minimum is 1180, whereas the selected rational point gives -419.
findings.dependency: Proposition 4.1 -> Proposition 1.9 -> Theorem 1.5. Invalid core proof branch, without disproving these conclusions.
findings.counterevidence: F only takes even values, so it is not a counterexample to the main nonrepresentation theorem. Nonnegativity does not exclude it.
findings.repair_boundary: Changing integer q to rational or rounding is insufficient; g2 grows quadratically. No general repair verified.

independent_verification.original_claim: p13 after (4.3) asserts integral q,h in g1=2g2 q+h, deg h<=1; p14 chooses v=-q(u) and concludes integer infimum -infinity when D(u)->+infinity.
independent_verification.assumptions: F=16(u^2+(2u+1)v)^2-u(u+1) has integer coefficients, degree4, F(0,0)=0, PSD F4=16u^2(u+2v)^2. H=u is primitive; G4=16(u+2v)^2 and G3=32v(u+2v) are integral quadratics neither divisible by H; G3 has distinct linear factors and no prohibited square divisor. Gcd(tildeF4,F3)=u(u+2v); gcd with F2=16v^2-u^2 is1. F2 is positive on both leading zero directions and cubic/quartic multiplicities are1/2. g2=16(2u+1)^2>0 for every integeru. Thus both explicit Proposition4.1 assumptions and relevant earlier reductions hold.
independent_verification.independent_proof: Expansion gives g1=32u^2(2u+1), g0=16u^4-u(u+1), D=u(u+1). Unique rational division gives q=u/2-1/4 and h=16u+8. Since q=(2u-1)/4 is nonintegral for every integeru, no integral subsequence supplies the selected v. h^2/(4g2)=1 gives the off-lattice value 1-u(u+1). For u=2k>=0, Q=(4k+1)(v+k)-k has least absolute integer residue k. For u=2k+1>=1, Q=(4k+3)(v+k)+(k+1) has least absolute residue k+1. Hence F>=3u^2-u>0 for u>=1 and F(0,v)=16v^2. The exact involution Q(-u-1,1-v)=Q(u,v), with u(u+1) invariant, covers all negativeu. Infimum on Z^2 is0. At u20 nearest integer v=-10 gives1180, while v=-39/4 gives-419. Own Fraction calculation exited0; universal nonnegativity follows from the analytic proof, not finite tests.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The polynomial takes only even values, so it is not a counterexample to the nonrepresentation theorem. The failure remains even under global integer nonnegativity; that cannot be an implicit exclusion.
independent_verification.impact: Proposition4.1 is explicitly used for Proposition1.9 (pp3,12), which joins1.7-1.9 to prove Theorem1.5. The unbounded-D branch makes a demonstrated false core inference. Major is justified independently of whether the overall dichotomy can be reproved.
independent_verification.repair_limits: Replacing integral by rational does not restore integer evaluation; rounding can cost order u^2 since g2 grows quadratically. No general replacement branch established.

findings.status: confirmed missing hypothesis in auxiliary statement
findings.claim: F>=C B^3 outside shrinking neighborhoods of common real zero directions of tilde F4 and F3.
assumptions_checked: linked: gcd(tilde G4,G3)=x^2 and gcd with G2 is 1
findings.decisive_evidence: G(-n^2,n)=n^2 and G/B^3=1/[n(n^2+1)^(3/2)] tends to zero.
findings.impact: Literal lemma omits quartic zero directions not shared by cubic. The example is already unbounded below along (-n,0), so no material damage to intended bounded-below target demonstrated.
findings.repair_boundary: Sufficient condition: all quartic real zero directions in Xi; local multiplicity bound and large neighborhood constant dominate cubic. Bounded-below reduction yields the condition by Lemma 2.5 reasoning.

independent_verification.original_claim: Section3 p6 defines Xi by simultaneous real zeros of tildeF4 and F3; Lemma3.1 p7 asserts F(Bcos theta,Bsin theta)>=C1 B^3 for all angles outside shrinking Xi neighborhoods, B sufficiently large by p3 convention.
independent_verification.assumptions: G=x^2y^2+x^3+y^2 is an integer quartic with G(0,0)=0, PSD leading form, gcd(tildeG4,G3)=x^2 and gcd with G2=y^2 equal1. Section3's actual assumptions do not state global boundedness below. Xi has x=0 directions; y=0 is an unshared leading zero direction.
independent_verification.independent_proof: At (-n^2,n), G=n^6-n^6+n^2=n^2>0 and B=n sqrt(n^2+1). Thus G/B^3=1/[n(n^2+1)^(3/2)]->0, whereas angles converge to the negative x axis, away from Xi and its shrinking neighborhoods. Positive-value restriction does not rescue the lemma.
independent_verification.counterevidence: G(-n,0)=-n^3 is unbounded below, so this already satisfies the alternative intended by the main nonrepresentation argument. No core target failure is established.
independent_verification.repair: Require all real leading zero directions to belong to Xi. Near multiplicity2r zeros, F4/B4 is bounded below by a positive constant times angular distance^(2r); outside c B^(-1/(2r)) neighborhoods the quartic lower bound is const*c^(2r) B^3. A sufficiently large c dominates the bounded cubic term, and compactness controls remaining angles. Moreover if a leading zero has nonzero cubic term, Dirichlet approximants with transverse linear form O(1/radius) give F4=O(1), |F3| comparable radius^3, lower terms O(radius^2); reversing sign forces negative divergence, as in the actual Lemma2.5 proof on p5. Thus a global bounded-below reduction supplies the needed condition.
independent_verification.impact: Literal auxiliary statement needs qualification; the report's Minor and explicit preliminary-reduction boundary are supported.

findings.claim: deg tilde Q2=0 if and only if deg R2=deg Q2=0.
assumptions_checked: K-d2=x^3-y is geometrically irreducible of genus zero
findings.decisive_evidence: tilde R2=-x^3 and tilde Q2=-1, despite deg R2=3.
findings.impact: False intermediate equivalence; does not refute Lemma 6.8 because F(x,x^3)=x is unbounded below.
findings.repair_boundary: Treat rational polynomial graph y=P(x). If one integral point exists, clearing coefficient denominators preserves integrality along an arithmetic progression in both signs. Only this subcase repaired.

independent_verification.original_claim: p24 asserts deg tildeQ2=0 iff deg R2=deg Q2=0 after the rational parametrization and (6.2).
independent_verification.assumptions: F=x(x^3-y+1), F4=x4>=0, gcd(tildeF4,F3,F2,F1)=gcd(x4,0,-xy,x)=x has degree1, as allowed in Lemma6.8 p22. K=x3-y+1 is primitive cubic, a=1,b=0. Choose C=d1=d2=1; K-d2=x3-y is geometrically irreducible genus0. Valid parametrization R1=t,Q1=1,R2=t3,Q2=1, with coprime pairs; r=v=1,s=u=0 and m=3.
independent_verification.independent_proof: The exact substitution t=(s-vx)/(ux-r)=x and factor (ux-r)^m=-1 give tildeR2=-x3 and tildeQ2=-1. Thus the denominator has degree0 while R2 has degree3. Along this curve F(x,x3)=x, so the target negative-value alternative holds.
independent_verification.repair: For the missed rational-polynomial graph y=P(x), let M clear all coefficients and suppose P(x0) is integral at an integerx0. Then P(x0+Mk)-P(x0) is integral for every integerk by the binomial expansion; this arithmetic progression extends in both signs. Since a*d2!=0 in the source setting, F=(ax+b)d2 is unbounded below on one sign. This repairs this subcase, not all geometric reductions.
independent_verification.impact: False subsidiary equivalence with a verified polynomial-graph repair; no counterexample to Lemma6.8 or the main theorem.
